A 40-year-old female patient visits her PCP with complaints of left facial pain that began the previous
day. The pain is described as stinging, burning, and continuous, without exacerbation during jaw
movement or mastication. Her medical history includes hyperlipidemia, multiple sclerosis (with a flare 5
weeks ago treated with prednisone), and chickenpox in childhood. Current medications include
simvastatin and glatiramer acetate. Physical examination reveals a temperature of 99.9°F (37.7°C),
blood pressure 147/95 mmHg, pulse 70/min, and respirations 18/min. The face shows no visible rash

or skin alterations. There is marked pain on gentle palpation of the left cheek and mandible, though jaw
mobility remains intact. Which medication would be most effective in preventing this patient's pain from
becoming chronic? Answer Choices: (A) Valacyclovir (B) Lidocaine patches (C) Intravenous
methylprednisolone (D) Oral acyclovir (E) Pregabalin (F) Carbamazepine (G) Topical corticosteroids
(H) Gabapentin (I) Oral prednisone (J) Amitriptyline
 A. Amitriptyline
B. Valacyclovir
